We made a preliminary examination of those cities with specifically defined commercial zones set forth in 49 CFR 1048.1 et seq., and concluded that the proposed formula would not adequately describe the commercial zones of at least nine cities. Consistent with the principles discussed above, we redescribed the zones for these cities along readily identifiable lines, in order to assure that no unintended contraction of commercial zone limits would occur by application of the proposed formula. The redescribed zones were set forth in the notice attached to the Interim Report. We invited comments of interested parties concerning these cities and any other cities which are similarly situated to those set forth in the notice. We stated our intention to formulate appropriate descriptions for such cities along readily identifiable boundaries. Interested parties were requested to submit clear maps demonstrating the limits of the commercial zones they suggest and to provide the Commission with economic data in support of such suggestions.
In response to this request, several interested parties pointed out that the proposed definitions of the Beaumont, Tex., and Lake Charles, La., commercial zones omit areas which are presently within these zones. The Beaumont parties complain that a portion of Orange County, Tex., which is presently a part of the Beaumont zone is excluded from the zone by the proposed section 1048.1 of the regulations.
